newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto greets new Thai premier.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto greets new Thai premier.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto congratulated Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh on Thursday on his November election victory and said his visit to Jakarta reflected the good relations between the two countries.
Chavalit arrived at Jakarta's Halim Perdanakusuma airbase for a two-day visit and talks with Suharto, the region's elder statesman.

The Thai leader was greeted by an artillery salute at the presidential palace in central Jakarta, and then had a formal courtesy visit with Suharto, who will be hosting a state banquet in the evening.
State Secretary Murdiono told reporters Suharto congratulated Chavalit on his election and expressed his appreciation that the Thai leader's first overseas visit should be to Indonesia.
"This reflects the good relations between the two countries. Both countries highly value their relationship and cooperation," Murdiono quoted Suharto as saying.

Diplomatic sources said the visit was primarily a courtesy call, following a custom of new leaders of members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to call first on fellow ASEAN states.
Suharto, Indonesia's leader since the mid-1960s, is a co-founder of ASEAN and one of the world's longest-serving heads of state.
ASEAN comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam.
Chavalit has personal ties to Indonesia. His wife Phanklua was born here and emigrated to Thailand.
Thai diplomatic sources said there were no outstanding issues between Bangkok and Jakarta.
"They will have open-ended discussions, but there are no particular issues," one source said. The talks would cover bilateral relations and cooperation in various areas.

Murdiono said he could not predict what would be discussed during formal talks on Friday morning before the Thai party leaves for home, but he said there were no fundamental problems between the two countries.
